news.title:
Adani Green's shares rose 45% in 2026, driven by robust capacity additions, strong financials, and execution.
Net debt surged to ₹91,000 cr in FY26; high capex and debt-to-EBITDA remain investor concerns, despite growth prospects.

Adani Green Energy promoter sold 1.3% stake for ₹3,246 cr to Adani Infra, reducing its holding to 5.05%.
Shares rose 3% to ₹1,532 on NSE as the transaction bolstered confidence in the group's renewable energy focus.
ADANIGREEN: Joint Venture And Governance Moves Will Support Future Earnings Visibility
news.body: Analysts have kept the price target for Adani Green Energy unchanged at ₹1,570, citing relatively steady assumptions around revenue growth, profit margins, and future P/E expectations as the main factors behind this stance. What's in the News Adani Green Energy has scheduled a board meeting on April 24, 2026, to consider fourth quarter FY 2025-26 results, board level appointments and reappointments, changes in senior management, and matters related to joint statutory auditors.

news.title: Full year 2026 earnings: EPS and revenues miss analyst expectations
news.body: Full year 2026 results: EPS: ₹9.65 (up from ₹8.38 in FY 2025). Revenue: ₹129.9b (up 14% from FY 2025). Net income: ₹15.8b (up 19% from FY 2025). Profit margin: 12% (in line with FY 2025). Revenue missed analyst estimates by 2.4%. Earnings per share (EPS) also missed analyst estimates by 15%. Revenue is forecast to grow 25% p.a. on average during the next 3 years, compared to a 16% growth forecast for the Renewable Energy industry in India. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has increased by 17% per year whereas the company’s share price has increased by 14% per year.

news.title: Third quarter 2026 earnings: Revenues exceed analysts expectations while EPS lags behind
news.body: Third quarter 2026 results: ₹0.38 loss per share (down from ₹2.92 profit in 3Q 2025). Revenue: ₹26.2b (up 11% from 3Q 2025). Net loss: ₹410.0m (down 108% from profit in 3Q 2025). Revenue exceeded analyst estimates by 3.5%. Earnings per share (EPS) missed analyst estimates. Revenue is forecast to grow 19% p.a. on average during the next 3 years, compared to a 16% growth forecast for the Renewable Energy industry in India. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has increased by 23% per year but the company’s share price has fallen by 20% per year, which means it is significantly lagging earnings.
